question: With reference to the Supreme Court's decision of September 2026 in the election dispute concerning the Malegaon Central Assembly constituency, consider the following statements: 1. The Court upheld the High Court's view that performing a 'dua' at a campaign gathering did not by itself amount to an appeal for votes on the ground of religion under Section 123(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1951. 2. The election petition in this case was filed directly before the Supreme Court. 3. Proof of a corrupt practice under Section 123 is a ground on which an election may be declared void. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih (25 Sep 2026) upheld the Bombay High Court's dismissal, holding that a dua is not a religious appeal under s.123(3). Statement 2 is wrong: election petitions are tried by the High Court (s.80A) and only the appeal lies to the Supreme Court (s.116A). Statement 3 is correct: a proven corrupt practice is a ground under s.100(1)(b).
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Elections and Representation of the People Act
micro_topic: Section 123(3) RPA 1951 - religious appeal as corrupt practice (Malegaon Central case, 2026)

question: With reference to the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, consider the following statements: 1. It enters into force on 20 October 2026 and gives Indian exports duty-free access on all of New Zealand's tariff lines. 2. India has excluded dairy products from its tariff concessions under the agreement. 3. It is the first free trade agreement under which India has secured a specific investment commitment from its partner. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The FTA (signed 27 April 2026) enters into force on 20 October 2026 with 100% duty-free access for Indian exports, and India has fully excluded dairy. Statement 3 is wrong: New Zealand's US$20 billion over 15 years pledge is India's second such commitment, after the EFTA TEPA (US$100 billion over 15 years).
subject: International Relations
micro_topic: India-New Zealand FTA - entry into force, dairy exclusion, investment pledge

question: With reference to the Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR) launched in September 2026, consider the following statements: 1. It is the sixth cycle of the evaluation and covers all 58 tiger reserves of India. 2. Solid waste management has been added as a separate evaluation criterion. 3. The evaluation framework is adapted from that of the IUCN World Commission on Protected Areas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: All three are correct. The sixth cycle (after 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022) covers all 58 reserves, adds solid waste management (from forest chowkis, tourism and rescue centres) as a new criterion, and uses the IUCN-WCPA framework. It is conducted by NTCA with the Wildlife Institute of India.
subject: Environment
micro_topic: Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves (MEE-TR 2026)

question: With reference to the SAT-SAAW systems contracted by the Ministry of Defence in September 2026, consider the following statements: 1. The weapon has been developed by DRDO, and the contract for its production has been signed with Bharat Dynamics Limited. 2. It is an air-launched precision-guided glide weapon designed to strike airfield infrastructure from stand-off distances. 3. It has been procured under the 'Buy (Global)' category of the Defence Acquisition Procedure. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: SAT-SAAW was developed by DRDO's Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad, and BDL is building 160 units under a Rs 810.79 crore contract. It is a 125-kg-class stand-off glide weapon for runways, radars and bunkers. Statement 3 is wrong: it was procured under Buy (Indian-IDDM), the highest-priority indigenous category.
subject: Science & Technology

question: With reference to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) September 2026 draft on 'analogue paneer', consider the following statements: 1. FSSAI functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution. 2. The draft proposes to amend the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, to prohibit paneer made of constituents not derived from milk. 3. FSSAI is a statutory body established under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: FSSAI comes under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, not Consumer Affairs, so statement 1 is wrong. The draft (published 22 September 2026, 60-day consultation) amends the 2011 Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales Regulations under Section 92 of the FSS Act, 2006. Analogue products would have to drop the word 'paneer'.
subject: Society
micro_topic: FSSAI draft on analogue paneer; FSSAI's statutory basis

question: With reference to election disputes and corrupt practices under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, consider the following statements: 1. An election petition challenging the election of a Member of Parliament or a State Legislature is tried, at first instance, by the High Court. 2. In Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen (2017), a seven-judge Bench of the Supreme Court held that the expression 'his religion' in Section 123(3) covers the religion of the voters as well. 3. An election petition may be presented at any time within one year of the date of declaration of the result. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: The High Court is the election tribunal (s.80A), and Abhiram Singh (2017, 4:3 majority) read 'his religion' to include the religion of the candidate, the agent and the voter. Statement 3 is wrong: the limit is 45 days from the declaration of the result (s.81).
subject: Polity & Governance
theme: Elections and Representation of the People Act
micro_topic: Election petitions - forum, limitation; Abhiram Singh case

question: Consider the following statements regarding the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA): 1. It is a statutory body constituted under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. 2. It is chaired by the Prime Minister. 3. A tiger reserve is notified by the State Government on the recommendation of the NTCA. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
explanation: NTCA was constituted in 2006 by amending the WPA 1972 (s.38L), and a State Government notifies a tiger reserve on NTCA's recommendation (s.38V). Statement 2 is wrong: NTCA is chaired by the Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
subject: Environment
micro_topic: NTCA - statutory basis, chair, notification of tiger reserves
